name: The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology Guangzhou
overview:
Additional Programme Specifics

  • Students with a Chinese passport are not allowed to apply to this university


The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology (Guangzhou)

Officially established in June 2022, The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology (Guangzhou) is a legally-independent educational institution co-established by the Mainland and Hong Kong. HKUST(GZ) will explore new frontiers in cross-disciplinary education and innovate pedagogies. By doing so, HKUST(GZ) will play a constructive role in cultivating forward-looking talents with global vision, promoting the higher education reform at a national level, and accelerating educational collaboration between Hong Kong and Mainland as well as the development of the Greater Bay Area (GBA).

  • College System

HKUST (GZ) adopts the collegiate system for its undergraduate education, where colleges and hubs collaborate with each other

  • Innovative Teaching

Inline with the individualized approach, undergraduate teaching has been transformed from a traditional teaching model into an innovative modular one.

  • Multi-modal Learning

The "immersive teaching" and "group project-based learning" models reshape the teacher's role from a traditional lecturer to an actual coach and mentor.

  • Intergrating Ressources

Under the Unified HKUST-Complementary Campuses framework, HKUST and HKUST (GZ) share resources with each other such as laboratories, libraries, courses and teachers, etc.
administrative:
1. Application Documents

You will be working directly with the partner university regarding your application.

Your host university may ask for the following documents:

  • A copy of valid passport
  • Cover letter/Personnal Statement
  • Enrollment Certificate with expected graduation date (ask your IAFF team)
  • TEPitech
  • Official transcript from High School
  • Nomination and an academic referee
  • Guardianship letter notarized at the local Chinese embassy (who were born after April 30, 2008)
  • One colored bareheaded photo with white background
  • No criminal record notarized by the local Chinese embassy or apostilled by the competent authorities (English and Chinese Versions)
  • Bank deposit certificate (Amount RMB100,000 or above)

If you documents are in other languages than English and Chinese, please prepare an official English translation of the documents or an English translation endorsed by your school.

All applicants should register and submit online applications via the HKUST(GZ) Online Application System (Click to Apply). The online application fee is RMB150 (2026/27 entry, the amount may vary). Please note that the application fee, once paid, is non-refundable and non-transferable irrespective of whether the application is successful or not.


Scholarship

All applicants will be automatically considered for admissions scholarships without extra application. Details of admissions scholarships awarded will be released with admission offers.   

Moreover, international students can apply for Guangdong Government Outstanding International Student Scholarship every year. 



2. Reception of the letter of admission

Once your application has been accepted, you will receive your acceptance letter signed by HKUST (GZ).

The letter of acceptance might be required by the Immigration Office to proceed with your visa application.



3. Visa

I- Before your arrival

As an international student, you must apply for a Student Visa before coming to China to start your courses. Otherwise, you will not be able to register for your study at HKUST(GZ). Refer to Chinese Visa Application Service Center for more information about the visa application: https://www.visaforchina.cn/globle/

II-During your studies

International students with long-term study purpose in China shall hold X1 visa and apply for residence permits for study within 30 days after entry. A fine of 500RMB per day will be applied for visa expiration. Please note that the University will only be allowed to apply for a residence permit for officially registered students.

III-Step by step guidance

1) Prepare the required material for visa application

2) Make an appointment in Office of Student Affairs (Room 203, 2nd Floor, Building C2) and get the Residence Permit Application Form.

3) Go to the immigration office as the appointment paper shows to apply for visa

a.Entry and Exit Reception Hall for Foreigners of Guangzhou Public Security Bureau: No.155, Jiefangnan Road, Yuexiu District；

b.Nansha Talent One-stop Government Affairs Center: The 2nd floor of Nansha International Talent Port Building, No. 167 Haibin Road, Nansha District;

4) Collect your passport from immigration office on the designated date

5) Update your visa information in the police station with passport and obtain the new Accommodation Registration Form for Visitors

6) Submit the copy of registration form to Office of Student Affairs (Room 203. 2nd Floor, Building C2)

IV-What you need to prepare

1)   First application for Residence Permit for Study

a.    Original passport and copy of valid passport and the visa used in the latest entry

b.    A valid Accommodation Registration Form for Visitors in Guangzhou

c.    Physical examination result issued by Guangzhou International Travel Health Care Center

d.    Receipt of China Visa Photograph for Foreigners in Guangdong Province and one photo

e.    Copy of Admission Letter

f.     Original Visa Application Form for Study in China (JW202)

2)   Extension of Residence Permit for Study

a.    Original passport and copy of valid passport and the visa used in the latest entry

b.    A valid Accommodation Registration Form for Visitors in Guangzhou

c.    Receipt of China Visa Photograph for Foreigners in Guangdong Province and one photo



4. Insurance and Health

It is imperative that you take out insurance that will cover you for your medical and hospital expenses, repatriation and accompanied by civil liability. International insurance must cover the entire period of your studies in the country. Insurance costs are the responsibility of each student.

To take out international insurance, the market is quite open. Please click here for more information.

For more information, check the country's health forms here: Partir en Chine : informations et vaccins voyage - Institut Pasteur

You can also check the French Ministry of Foreign Affairs' website: Chine - Santé | France Diplomatie

Note: It is advisable to register on the French register established outside France and to report to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs via the Ariane platform: https://pastel.diplomatie.gouv.fr/fildariane/dyn/public/login.html.
accomodation:
On-campus accommodation:

The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology (Guangzhou) Phase One has seven buildings used as student dormitories, which can accommodate about 3,500 students in total. The student dormitory has 3 types of rooms, including multi-bedroom suites (6-bedroom unit, 7-bedroom unit, and 8-bedroom unit), 1B1B units, and Studios.

  • 6-bedroom apartment: 6 single rooms with a shared living room and 2 bathrooms (RMB2500 /Year)  
  • 8-bedroom apartment: 8 single rooms with a shared living room and 2 bathrooms (RMB2000 /Year)


Multi-bedroom Suites :

  • Independent Bedroom：Each student has a private bedroom, equipped with beds (including mattresses), desks, chairs, and wardrobes, which are simple and have good privacy.
  • Shared living and dining room： Spacious and bright living and dining room in the dormitory, equipped with leisure sofas, wooden coffee tables, wooden tables, and dining chairs, etc., providing a space for social sharing among roommates.
  • Kitchen： The kitchen is equipped with range hoods, double-door refrigerators, induction cookers, microwave ovens, electric kettles, and other home appliances.
  • Bathroom & Washstand： Multiple-bedroom suites are equipped with separate toilets and bathrooms, as well as two sets of double washstands.

There is a laundry room on the first floor of the student dormitory, equipped with washing machines and dryers, to provide students with convenience in life.

For more information please check: Student Dormitories – The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology (Guangzhou)

Important notes

  • Presence in class is compulsory, under penalty of loss of visa and repatriation to France at the student's expense (impact on credits).
  • The courses are most likely more academic than at EPITECH.
  • The course list is given for information only. It can change from year to year.
  • If a course is not available when you arrive on site, EPITECH cannot be held responsible for it.
  • Any Tech 4 abroad involves an EIP! Take advantage of the free slots you will have to advance it.
cost:
Financial overview (4th year Epitech)

  • You must pay the tuition fees for the 4th year of EPITECH, as well as the re-registration fees and related fees.
  • Epitech covers the tuition fees required by HKUST (GZ).
  • Other costs at your expense include: travel, accommodation on site, insurance, and everyday expenses (books, food, transport, etc.).


Other Expenses

  • Roundtrip flights: from 800€
  • Medical insurance: 150€
  • Additional insurance: 300-600€ depending on the coverage
  • Visa: between 110-130€
  • Medical examinations in China: 50-100€
  • Residence permit application: 100€ (one year)
  • Application fee: RMB150 (19€)


Estimated monthly budget

Please check the Numbeo website to compare the cost of living between your city of origin and your city of exchange. Please note that everyone's budget will be different according to one's lifestyle.

Additional information

  • Get a good VPN. Internet restrictions in China can be tricky, so a reliable VPN is essential. Students have mentioned the following three, which work consistently well: MullvadVPN, Let’sVPN, and ChamVPN. Make sure to install and test them before arriving in China, as VPN websites are usually blocked there.
  • The Trip.com app is extremely useful, you can book everything from flights and trains to hotels and activities directly from it. It supports English, accepts international payment cards, and usually offers better prices than foreign apps.
  • Open a Chinese bank account. This is extremely important. Many popular Chinese platforms such as Taobao (the main online shopping website) don’t always accept foreign cards, and WeChat Pay or Alipay charge small fees when using international cards. Having a local bank account allows you to transfer money easily from your foreign account, convert euros to yuan, and avoid extra charges. It’s also much more convenient in daily life: without a Chinese card, you can’t send money to friends through WeChat, which makes it complicated to split bills or reimburse someone after a restaurant or a trip. Opening an account at ICBC, Bank of China, or China Construction Bank is usually straightforward, as long as you bring your passport and student card.
  • Take slow trains to travel around China; for long trips, take a sleeping train to make the journey feel quicker. China has excellent and affordable high-speed trains, making it easy to visit places like Shanghai, Xi’An, Hangzhou, Chengdu, or Harbin.
  • Download WeChat and Alipay, they’re essential for daily life in China (payments, communication, deliveries, etc.). You can link them to an international bank card like Wise or Revolut. Other useful apps include: Taobao (equivalent of Amazon), Tencen map or Gaode map, Meituan, Didi (taxis—don’t take the one at the airport!), Xiao Hong Shu (equivalent of Instagram), Ctrip.
